nodes.name: Load Campaign + Niche
nodes.notes: One read per run. Campaign settings - ICP band, thresholds, daily targets, follow-up offsets - all come from here, never from node parameters.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_campaign_id: $json.id || $json.campaign_id, p_stage: 'SCRAPED', p_limit: $json.batch_size || 25, p_worker: 'wf02-clean-dedupe', p_stale_minutes: 20, p_max_retries: 3 }) }}

nodes.name: Claim SCRAPED Leads
nodes.notes: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so parallel executions never hand the same lead to two workers. A claim older than 20 minutes is treated as abandoned and reissued, which is how a crashed run resumes instead of stranding leads at SCRAPED.

nodes.name: Fetch Company Record
nodes.notes: One read per claimed lead. Swap for a single ?id=in.(...) read if batch sizes grow beyond a few hundred.

nodes.name: Apply Cleaning Rules
nodes.notes: Rules come from config/cleaning.json, inlined at build time. Edit that file and rebuild to change what is filtered - no node edits.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ niche_id: $('Load Campaign + Niche').first().json.niche_id, business_model: $('Load Campaign + Niche').first().json.niche?.business_model }) }}

nodes.name: Tag Company With Niche
nodes.notes: Only the niche tagging. The cleaning flags travel on the advance_lead detail into the activity log - writing them here would overwrite companies.raw, which holds the provider payload.

nodes.name: Store Cleaning Flags
nodes.notes: Niche keyword hits, personal-account signals and location reasoning. Qualification scores niche fit from these, so they must survive the cleaning run.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ disqualified_reason: $json.reasons.join(", "), qualified: false, notes: "Dropped at cleaning: " + $json.reasons.join(", ") }) }}

nodes.name: Classify Failure
nodes.notes: Uses the same classifier as the test suite: 429 backs off, 5xx retries, 401/422 dead-letters immediately.
